course_name_original: I.C. SIGNAL ANALYSIS AND STATISTICAL METHODS FOR BIOENGINEERING (TO0037)
course_name_en: I.C. SIGNAL ANALYSIS AND STATISTICAL METHODS FOR BIOENGINEERING
prerequisites: Knowledge of elements of physiology, analysis and physics
Knowledge of rudiments of Matlab coding
Functions of two or more variables

learning_outcomes.text: Interpret results from a physiological perspective
Implement simple algorithms in MATLAB or Python

syllabus_topics: Techniques for the acquisition of biomedical signals
Techniques for the processing of biomedical signals
Applications: ECG, EMG, EEG, PPG, fNIRS
Examples: Analysis of RR variability in the ECG
Applications: EEG Bands (delta, theta, alpha, beta, gamma)
Low-pass, high-pass, and notch filter design
Applications to Dynamic EEG and EMG
Feature Extraction and Introduction to Pattern Recognition
Feature Extraction in Time and Frequency
Connection to Medical Devices and AI

assessment_methods.method: Written test with multiple-choice, open-ended questions, and simple problem-solving

assessment_rules: For the Signal Analysis module, the final exam is a 120-minute written test assessing the application of methodological knowledge, with grades from 18 to 30/30 (with honors for correctly answering all questions). For the Statistics module, the examination consists of periodic assessments with two written tests and one oral examination, where the final grade is the arithmetic mean of the three grades. Alternatively, for students not taking partial assessments, the examination consists of one written test and one oral examination.
bibliography: Practical Guide for Biomedical Signals Analysis Using Machine Learning Techniques: A MATLAB® Based Approach. Abdulhamit Subasi. Elsevier Academic Press
R.M. Rangayyan, Biomedical signal analysis, IEEE Press, 2002
Handouts and materials provided by the teacher on the e-learning platform.
De Groot, M. Schervish, Probability and Statistics, Addison Wesley 4th ed.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Biomedica (Biomedical Engineering), classe L-9 R Ingegneria industriale
